text:
Minah: quick brain-dump — I'm proposing a signal-attenuation layer between canary metrics and the fallback actuator. aim: avoid noisy, single-spike triggered rollbacks. TL;DR: smooth -> attenuate -> score -> circuit decision.
Jorge: can you sketch the inputs? e.g., error-rate, p95 latency, model-quality deltas?
Minah: yep. inputs = {error_rate, p95_lat, model_quality_change, user_error_fraction}. each gets a weight + short sliding window smoothing. then attenuator reduces sensitivity for tiny bursts.
Aisha: love the idea. think we need to be explicit about window sizes per metric. model_quality_change should have a longer half-life (mins->hours) while latency can be seconds.
Minah: agreed. rough defaults I used in the doc: latency: 30s EWMA, error_rate: 60s EWMA, quality: 30m average. weights are configurable per route.
Jorge: how does this interact with session affinity? we must not flip a user's session mid-request.
Lev: keep routing decisions at request boundaries. the attenuator should emit a score, and the router checks `inflight_affinity` before switching. if affinity locked, schedule soft-diversion on next request.
Minah: exact. router contract: `canSwitch(sessionId) -> boolean`. if false, we queue the session for soft-diversion. would like a clear operator override to force immediate swap.
Aisha: what about multi-variant partial fallback (e.g., degrade to quantized model instead of full fallback)?
Minah: plan supports graded actions: percentages, degrade-mode, full-fallback. policy example attached below.
Minah: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  type: attenuated
  smoothing_windows:
    p95_latency: 30s
    error_rate: 60s
    quality_delta: 30m
  weights:
    p95_latency: 0.3
    error_rate: 0.4
    quality_delta: 0.3
  thresholds:
    warn: 0.25
    divert: 0.5
    circuit_open: 0.8
  actions_by_threshold:
    warn: notify+trace
    divert: route 20% -> fallback_variant
    circuit_open: route 100% -> fallback_variant + page_oncall
  cooldown: 5m
```
Jorge: code looks sane. how do we prevent cascading handoffs when multiple routes hit threshold concurrently?
Aisha: need global budget per cluster + per-customer budget. also prefer vertical isolation: only divert traffic for tenants with signals. global budget prevents mass shift.
Lev: +1 on per-tenant budget. also implement a small randomized jitter when applying percent diversions to avoid thundering herd.
Minah: another concern: metric disagreement. latency spikes sometimes without quality regressions. attenuator should allow each metric to veto or endorse with monotonicity. e.g., model_quality_delta has veto weight x2 for safety-critical routes.
Jorge: observability: what traces/metrics do we need?
Aisha: emit `attenuator_score`, `attenuated_threshold_crossing`, `diversion_action`, `circuit_state`, plus histograms for decision latency. tie to request IDs for debugging.
Minah: proposal includes a decision trace object saved for N requests to help postmortem. it contains the raw weighted inputs + final score + action.
Lev: implement kill-switch: operator can pin `router.policy.force_fallback=true` at route level. also add a dry-run mode that logs diversion decisions but doesn't actuate.
Minah: good. I also suggest an RFC follow-up to formalize APIs: `attenuator.evaluate(route, metrics) -> {score, reasons}` and `router.apply(route, score) -> action`. keep them small.
Jorge: do we want the attenuator centralized or sidecar per route?
Aisha: sidecar for low-latency quick decisions and local smoothing; central coordinator for global budgets and cross-route fusion. hybrid model seems best.
Minah: exactly: local attenuator(s) + central adjudicator that handles budgets and global circuit.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/attenuator-proto v0.1 -> staging (1729502699) :rocket:
Minah: thanks. next steps: I'll open RFC PR with API sketches, state diagrams, and a short sim harness to tune thresholds. any objections?
Jorge: no objections, please include failure-mode tests.
Aisha: also include a runbook snippet for oncall: how to interpret attenuator_score / emergency pin.
Lev: will give a quick review on the runtime integration bits.
Minah: great — I'll post the RFC link here once PR is up: <https://redwood.internal/rfcs/att-202> :thumbsup:
